energy_consumption.notes: December and January bills estimated due to a meter outage; gaps filled with 3-year average for those months.

zones.deficiencies_noted: Multiple gaps around recessed lighting penetrations; some batts compressed near eave baffles.
Completely uninsulated and air-sealed along entire perimeter.

insulation.llm_summary: The home's thermal envelope has significant weaknesses. The attic is under-insulated at R-19 versus the recommended R-49, with notable air leakage through lighting penetrations. The rim joist is entirely uninsulated and unsealed, representing the highest-priority improvement. Basement walls are adequate but could be upgraded. Overall air tightness at 9.2 ACH50 is well above the 3–5 ACH50 target for this climate zone.

units.deficiencies_noted: Heat exchanger shows hairline crack; recommend inspection by licensed HVAC technician before next heating season.

hvac.llm_summary: The 20-year-old furnace is operating below its rated efficiency and has a potentially hazardous heat exchanger crack requiring immediate professional evaluation. Replacement with a high-efficiency (95%+ AFUE) unit would significantly reduce heating costs. The central AC is in good condition but approaching end of useful life. Duct leakage at 280 CFM25 is moderate; sealing accessible joints in the basement could recover 10–15% of conditioned air.

windows_doors.llm_summary: Seven north- and east-facing single-pane windows account for significant heat loss during Wisconsin winters. Replacement with double-pane Low-E units or addition of interior storm panels would provide noticeable comfort improvements. Exterior door weatherstripping is worn on both doors and should be replaced as a low-cost, high-impact measure.

water_heating.llm_summary: The 12-year-old gas storage water heater is approaching end of life (typical lifespan 8–12 years). Its UEF of 0.62 is well below a modern heat pump water heater (UEF ~3.5). When replacement is needed, a heat pump water heater is strongly recommended. In the interim, adding pipe insulation on the first 6 feet of hot and cold connections and reducing the set point to 120 °F would yield modest savings.

appliances.name: refrigerator
appliances.notes: Side-by-side model; significantly less efficient than current top-freezer or French-door ENERGY STAR units.

appliances.name: clothes dryer
appliances.notes: Electric resistance dryer. Heat pump dryer would reduce consumption by ~30%.

appliances_lighting.llm_summary: Approximately 55% of lighting is still incandescent or CFL. Completing the LED retrofit is one of the lowest-cost, fastest-payback improvements available. The 15-year-old refrigerator consumes nearly double what a current ENERGY STAR model would use and should be prioritised for replacement.

recommendations.title: Replace aging gas furnace with high-efficiency model (95%+ AFUE)
recommendations.description: The existing 80% AFUE furnace is 20 years old and has a cracked heat exchanger. Replace with a 96% AFUE two-stage gas furnace. Prior to replacement, have a licensed HVAC technician inspect the heat exchanger for CO risk.
recommendations.available_incentives: Federal IRA 25C tax credit: 30% up to $600. WE Energies Focus on Energy rebate: up to $200.

recommendations.title: Air seal and insulate attic to R-49
recommendations.description: Dense-pack cellulose blown over existing batts after air-sealing all penetrations (recessed lights, top plates, plumbing chases) with fire-rated spray foam or caulk. Target final R-value of R-49.
recommendations.available_incentives: Federal IRA 25C tax credit: 30% up to $1,200. Focus on Energy Home Performance rebate: up to $400.

recommendations.title: Insulate and air seal rim joist with spray foam
recommendations.description: Apply 2-inch closed-cell spray polyurethane foam to the entire rim joist perimeter in the basement. This simultaneously insulates (R-12) and air seals in a single application.
recommendations.available_incentives: Included in Focus on Energy Home Performance rebate above.

recommendations.title: Replace single-pane north and east windows with double-pane Low-E
recommendations.description: Replace 7 single-pane windows (46 sq ft) with ENERGY STAR–certified double-pane Low-E units with U-factor ≤ 0.27 and SHGC ≤ 0.22.
recommendations.available_incentives: Federal IRA 25C tax credit: 30% up to $600 per year for windows.

recommendations.title: Replace storage tank water heater with heat pump water heater
recommendations.description: Install a 50-gallon heat pump water heater (UEF ~3.5) in the basement to replace the aging gas storage tank. Requires 10 sq ft of clear space and 700+ cubic feet of air volume.
recommendations.available_incentives: Federal IRA 25C tax credit: 30% up to $2,000. WE Energies rebate: $200.

recommendations.title: Complete LED lighting retrofit
recommendations.description: Replace all remaining incandescent and CFL bulbs with LED equivalents. Approximately 30 fixtures estimated.
recommendations.available_incentives: We Energies instant-discount LED bulbs at participating retailers.

executive_summary: This 1978 two-story home in Madison, WI scored a 4 out of 10 on the DOE Home Energy Score, indicating significant room for improvement. Annual energy costs of $2,381 are driven primarily by an aging, inefficient furnace and a poorly insulated envelope that leaks conditioned air at nearly twice the recommended rate. The six recommendations in this report — led by furnace replacement, attic air sealing/insulation, and rim joist insulation — could collectively reduce annual energy bills by approximately $1,595 and cut CO₂ emissions by over 2,900 kg per year. With available federal tax credits and utility rebates, net implementation costs can be reduced by 20–30%. We recommend addressing the furnace's cracked heat exchanger as an immediate safety priority.
